Thirteen weekly assignments, each a self-contained piece of the semester's
investigation using that week's tools. Every assignment states its goal
precisely and ships **reference checkpoints** — published totals, documented
counts, known facts — so you can know you are right before you submit.

## The thirteen assignments

Out on Thursday after class, due the following Thursday at 8:40 am. HW13 spans
Thanksgiving and gets two weeks.

::: {.tight-cols}
{{< include _hw_calendar.qmd >}}
:::

## Where to get them

Assignment starters and your submissions live in the **private GitHub
Classroom**. Invite links are posted on **Canvas** only — they are not on this
site, because each link creates a repository under your own account.

Every assignment ships a starter, and every week's starter includes a
known-good checkpoint of the running project. Falling behind one week never
snowballs.

## How to submit

| Assignments | How you submit |
|---|---|
| HW1 – HW3 | Browser upload — GitHub Classroom commits for you |
| HW4 – HW13 | git: clone, commit, push |

Session [7 · git & GitHub](sessions/07-git.qmd) is the changeover. Everything
before it you have been committing through the browser without needing to know
what a commit was.

## How they are graded

Every assignment is graded on the same four dimensions — reproduces, correct,
verified, craft — with weights that shift across the semester as verification
becomes the graded skill. The full rubric, the late-work policy, and the
disclosure requirement are in the [syllabus](syllabus.qmd#homework).
